belief: I have to hide who I really am to be accepted.
origins: Many learn early that certain parts of themselves, such as their faith, accent, interests, past, or feelings, bring teasing or rejection. They adapt, mask, and perform. Adults may spend years in groups where no one knows them well, exhausted by the effort and lonely despite being included.
teaches: God told Samuel, “Man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” Paul says, “Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God?” and that we speak “not in order to please men but God, who examines our hearts” (1 Thessalonians 2:4). The psalmist says, “I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” John writes, “If we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another.” Real fellowship happens when people know us. Not every setting is safe, so wisdom is needed, but the God who made us does not ask us to live behind a mask.
self_statements: If they knew the real me, they would reject me.
I have to act the part.
My true self is too much, or not enough.
I am only accepted because I pretend.
errors: Assuming I know how people would react.
Believing I must either mask completely or reveal everything.
Feeling exposed and concluding that it is dangerous.
questions: What parts of me do I hide, and why?
Who has seen more of the real me and still accepted me?
What is the difference between privacy and pretending?
What does God say about me?
What small part of myself could I reveal this week to a safe person?
truth: God made me as I am and knows me completely. I do not have to live behind a mask. With wise, safe people, I can reveal myself gradually and find acceptance that is real.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
log: Each week, note one way you were more honest and how it went.
actions: Write the parts of you that you mask.
Choose someone who has shown trustworthiness.
Thank God for making you as you are.
prayer: Lord, You know me completely. Give me courage to put down the mask with safe people and rest in Your love for who I am. Amen.
hw_questions: What is one thing I can share?
name_example: Sarah can write: “The Lord sees my heart, so I can be real.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I have to hide who I really am to be accepted.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
